observation.visible_scene: A close-up of a lit sparkler held at an angle against a deep-blue, layered ribbon-like 3D background (resembling a rendered wallpaper). The thin dark stick runs from the lower-left toward the upper-center, ending in a bright white-yellow burning tip that throws a starburst of glowing sparks in all directions. A persistent soft orange glow spot sits on the right side of the background, and the blue ribbons remain essentially stationary throughout.
visible_changes: The burning tip continuously emits sparks whose trajectories, lengths and star-shaped bursts differ from frame to frame (random, ongoing spark shower rather than a single event).
The overall brightness and size of the tip's core flicker, sometimes flaring into a larger white blob and sometimes tightening.
The stick's orientation and the tip's position shift slightly between frames (small tilts of the rod and minor drift of the tip near the upper-center), consistent with small hand-held movements.
Falling sparks and short streaks appear and vanish at varying locations around the tip and lower in the frame.
The orange background glow and the blue ribbon structure stay in the same positions, indicating no significant camera translation or zoom.
outside_clip_unknowns: Who or what holds the sparkler and how it is moved is not shown.
The origin of the orange background glow is not visible.
The start of ignition and the eventual burn-out of the sparkler lie outside this cropped segment.
Whether the background is a real surface or a rendered image is not determinable from the frames.
uncertain_details: The slight apparent shifts of the blue ribbons could be minor camera motion or just glare/reflection from the sparks; the evidence is insufficient to confirm camera movement.
The stick's motion is small and irregular, so precise hand gestures cannot be reconstructed.
